decisions.reason: As an older hardware launch with higher support and portfolio-complexity costs, and with no later market signal despite enough time for demand to become clearer, its option value now looks too limited to justify keeping it open.

As a software add-on tightly linked to the installed marking base, it is inexpensive to maintain and still fits the firm's digital variable-data and traceability direction, so keeping it remains the more attractive option.

Although by now the market should be clearer and hardware is costlier to carry than software, the product still addresses an important adjacent application in the core coding business, so management would more likely retain it than abandon it.
Because this app extends an existing decoding tool and supports serialization and traceability with relatively low carrying cost, real-options logic favors keeping it available.
An inline code verification system is strategically close to the firm's compliance and end-to-end traceability trajectory, so despite some uncertainty it is valuable to keep in the portfolio.
Print layout design software is a low-cost complement to the firm's coding equipment that can strengthen customer lock-in and common operation across systems, making continued retention likely.
